Start after [installation](installation.qmd). Q2D takes explicit cross-section
rectangles; it does not import a GDS, derive a slice from the Xmon snapshot or
infer a transmission line from a 3D picture. The public
[OrPen cross-section source](../examples.qmd#public-inputs) supplies this
specimen: 10 µm signal width, 10 µm gaps, 40 µm grounds, 0.2 µm metal thickness,
and a 200 µm wide, 500 µm thick substrate. These are model inputs.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import orpen_sc_pdk
from orpen_sc_pdk.materials import get_material_records
from scgsim.aedt import (
    MatrixRunControl, PdkMaterial, Q2dConductorSpec,
    Q2dRectangleSpec, Q2dSpec, prepare_handoff,
)

orpen_sc_pdk.activate()
records = get_material_records()
materials = {
    name: PdkMaterial(name, records[name]["material_kind"],
                      records[name]["is_superconducting"],
                      records[name]["aedt_library_name"])
    for name in ("vacuum", "Si", "Nb")
}
rectangles = (
    Q2dRectangleSpec("Substrate", (-100.0, -500.0), (200.0, 500.0), "Si"),
    Q2dRectangleSpec("Signal", (-5.0, 0.0), (10.0, 0.2), "Nb"),
    Q2dRectangleSpec("GroundLeft", (-55.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.2), "Nb"),
    Q2dRectangleSpec("GroundRight", (15.0, 0.0), (40.0, 0.2), "Nb"),
)
conductors = (
    Q2dConductorSpec("Signal", "SignalLine", ("Signal",), 0.2),
    Q2dConductorSpec("Ground", "ReferenceGround", ("GroundLeft", "GroundRight"), 0.2),
)
spec = Q2dSpec(
    project_name="public_cpw_q2d", design_name="CpwFiniteGroundQ2d",
    materials=materials, vacuum_material_id="vacuum",
    rectangles=rectangles, conductors=conductors,
    run_control=MatrixRunControl("Setup1", frequency_ghz=6.0, maximum_passes=3),
    region_padding_um=(100.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 100.0),
)
handoff = prepare_handoff(spec=spec, output_dir=Path(".artifacts/public-cpw-q2d"))
print(spec.to_payload())
print(handoff.spec_path, handoff.archive_path)
```

Rectangle origins and sizes are micrometres. Read each lower-left position and
size against the intended gaps; print the source spec before relying on native
geometry. The vacuum belongs to the Region, not an authored vacuum rectangle.
There is one `ReferenceGround` group covering both ground rectangles and at
least one `SignalLine`; every superconducting rectangle belongs to exactly one
group. The four-value Region padding uses **(-X, +X, -Y, +Y)**, unlike the
six-value native order in the 3D input lesson.

After [execution](execute.qmd), [resolve the full return](returned-results.qmd).
The accepted Q2D export behavior has one native `results/q2d/rlgc_matrix.csv`,
containing primary C, G, L and R blocks. `resolved.physics_results()` reads those
blocks without creating another normalized file. Native coupling or Spice
blocks can coexist without becoming extra primary matrices. The resolver binds
frequency, `LastAdaptive` solution, conductor order and per-unit-length units.

Per-unit-length capacitance is not a lumped Electrostatic capacitance, and a
Q2D cross-section is not the finite 3D Q3D experiment. Preserve those units and
scope when interpreting the result. Historical separate CG/RL and normalized
Q2D files are not emitted for new requests. The
[AEDT contract](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q2d-native-combined-matrix-export)
owns the exact export, historical readers and failure behavior; broader AEDT
semantics remain CONVERGING.
